_comment: Prompt-reduction rules for the commands this project actually runs, derived from 50 recent
session transcripts (2026-08-17).
WHY THIS FILE IS SHORT. .claude/settings.local.json already allows 'Bash' and 'PowerShell'
wholesale, so a missing allow-rule is almost never what causes a prompt here. What still
prompts is SANDBOX ESCALATION - a command that spawns processes, touches the network, or
writes outside the sandbox - and that is suppressed by an exact/prefix rule, not by the
blanket tool grant. Every entry above is one of those.
DELIBERATELY NOT LISTED:
- grep / cat / ls / head / tail / find / sort / wc and git status|log|diff|show|branch:
Claude Code auto-allows these, so a rule would be dead weight.
- 'dotnet run *' as a wildcard: that is arbitrary code execution. Only the three sanctioned
verification tools are listed, by project path. A fourth tool needs its own line - which
is the point.
2026-08-19 RESCAN. The two 'dotnet run' rules above were written WITHOUT a trailing ' *', and a
rescan of 50 transcripts found that all 184 real invocations carry extra arguments - '2>&1', a
redirect, or '-- --check'. So both rules had matched exactly ZERO calls since they were added.
Added the ' *' forms plus SkillCsvSeed (the CSV verifier CLAUDE.md requires before committing
skill work, 36 calls, never listed at all). Coverage: 164 of 184. Left out tools/ItemIds (5
calls) and one-off scratchpad .csproj probes - too rare to be worth an execution grant.
- rm / Remove-Item / taskkill / git add|commit|push|checkout|stash|mv: these MUTATE. The
ones already approved sit in settings.local.json where 'always allow' wrote them.
- python / perl / pwsh / npx and friends: arbitrary code execution.
Note 'dotnet build' IS a build, not a read-only command - it writes bin/obj and can run
MSBuild pre-build steps. It is here anyway because it is the single most frequent call in
the project by a wide margin and CLAUDE.md tells Claude to build freely. Remove the four
'dotnet build' lines if you would rather be asked.
